title: Airport Lighting, Markings & Signs
description: Key concepts from AIM Chapter 2 covering airport lighting systems, visual approach aids, runway/taxiway markings, and airport signs

cards.back:
• Provide transition from instrument to visual flight
• Precision runways: 2,400-3,000 feet
• Nonprecision runways: 1,400-1,500 feet
• May include sequenced flashing lights ('ball of light' effect)
• Various configurations: ALSF-1, ALSF-2, SSALR, MALSR, etc.

Memory aid: 'Red over White, You're Alright'

• All RED = Below glidepath (too low)
• Red over White = On glidepath (correct)
• All WHITE = Above glidepath (too high)

Normal glidepath: 3°
Visibility: 3-5 miles day, 20+ miles night

• Safe clearance: ±10° of extended centerline
• Range: 4 NM from threshold
• Don't initiate descent until visually aligned with runway
• VASI provides vertical guidance only
• Runway/runway lights provide lateral guidance

• Provides TWO visual glidepaths
• Lower path: Near & middle bars (normal 3°)
• Upper path: Middle & far bars (¼° higher)
• Upper path for high cockpit aircraft
• Ensures sufficient threshold crossing height
• Use appropriate glidepath for your aircraft type

Similar to VASI but uses single row of 4 lights:
• 4 WHITE = Too high
• 3 WHITE, 1 RED = Slightly high
• 2 WHITE, 2 RED = On glidepath
• 1 WHITE, 3 RED = Slightly low
• 4 RED = Too low

Usually on left side of runway

• Synchronized flashing lights at threshold
• Located on each side of runway
• Provides rapid identification of approach end
• Useful for:
 - Runway surrounded by other lighting
 - Low terrain contrast
 - Reduced visibility

• HIRL: High Intensity (variable control)
• MIRL: Medium Intensity (variable control)
• LIRL: Low Intensity (single setting)

Colors:
• White along edges
• Yellow last 2,000 ft or ½ runway (caution zone) on instrument runways
• End lights: Red toward runway, Green outward

Color progression from threshold:
• WHITE: Until last 3,000 feet
• ALTERNATING RED/WHITE: Next 2,000 feet
• ALL RED: Last 1,000 feet

• Spaced 50 feet apart
• On precision approach runways

• Two rows of light bars on each side of centerline
• Steady-burning white lights
• Start 100 feet beyond threshold
• Extend to 3,000 feet or runway midpoint
• Indicates touchdown zone in low visibility

• Color: Alternating GREEN and YELLOW
• Warn of runway environment or ILS critical area
• Lead-off: Guide aircraft exiting runway
• Lead-on: Guide aircraft entering runway
• Same fixtures, bidirectional

• Pulsing WHITE lights across runway
• Located at LAHSO hold short point
• ON only when LAHSO is in effect
• OFF when LAHSO not in effect
• Must stop before these lights if instructed to hold short

Runway Status Light System (Automated):

REL (Runway Entrance Lights):
• At taxiway/runway intersections
• Red = unsafe to enter

THL (Takeoff Hold Lights):
• On runway centerline
• Red = unsafe to take off

Does NOT substitute for ATC clearance!

Key microphone on CTAF within 5 seconds:
• 7 clicks = Highest intensity
• 5 clicks = Medium intensity
• 3 clicks = Lowest intensity

• Lights remain on for 15 minutes
• Available at uncontrolled airports
• All lighting systems on same frequency

• WHITE + GREEN = Lighted land airport
• WHITE + YELLOW = Lighted water airport
• GREEN + YELLOW + WHITE = Heliport
• WHITE (dual-peaked) + GREEN = Military airport

Flash rate: 24-30/min (airports), 30-45/min (heliports)

May indicate:
• Visibility < 3 statute miles, AND/OR
• Ceiling < 1,000 feet

CAUTION:
• Don't rely solely on beacon for weather
• May be photoelectric/timer controlled
• ATC may not have control
• Always verify weather independently

• Edge lights: BLUE
• Centerline lights: GREEN
• Clearance bar lights: YELLOW (3 in-pavement)
• Runway guard lights: YELLOW (flashing or in-pavement)
• Stop bar lights: RED (unidirectional)

NEVER cross a red illuminated stop bar, even if cleared by ATC!

• Red, unidirectional, in-pavement lights
• Across entire taxiway at holding position
• Used in low visibility (<1,200 RVR)
• If lights extinguish after crossing, HOLD and contact ATC

RUNWAY = WHITE markings
• Centerline, threshold, numbers, etc.

TAXIWAY = YELLOW markings
• Centerlines, edges, holding positions

HELIPAD = WHITE (red 'H' on white cross for hospitals)

1. VISUAL: Basic markings (centerline, numbers, threshold)

2. NONPRECISION INSTRUMENT: Visual + aiming point, threshold bars

3. PRECISION INSTRUMENT: All above + touchdown zone markings, side stripes

More markings = more capable runway

• Two broad white rectangular stripes
• Located ~1,000 feet from threshold
• On both sides of centerline
• Visual aiming point for landing
• Found on instrument runways

• Groups of 1, 2, or 3 bars
• Symmetrical about centerline
• Coded for distance in 500-ft increments
• Pattern: 1, 2, 3, 2, 1 bars
• Marks touchdown zone area
• On precision instrument runways

• White stripes across runway width
• Number of stripes indicates runway width:
 - 4 stripes = 60 ft
 - 6 stripes = 75 ft
 - 8 stripes = 100 ft
 - 12 stripes = 150 ft
 - 16 stripes = 200 ft

NORMAL: Single continuous yellow line (6-12 inches wide)

ENHANCED: Yellow dashes parallel to centerline
• Up to 150 ft before holding position
• Warning of approaching hold line
• Prepare to stop!

CONTINUOUS double yellow lines:
• Do NOT cross
• Separates taxiway from non-aircraft areas

DASHED double yellow lines:
• May cross
• Adjacent pavement is for aircraft use (apron)

• Four yellow lines: 2 solid, 2 dashed
• Solid lines on hold side
• MUST STOP at solid lines
• Aircraft not clear until ALL parts cross

Locations:
• Taxiway/runway intersection
• Runway/runway intersection
• Approach area holding position

• Yellow ladder pattern marking
• Hold here when ILS in use
• Protects ILS signal integrity
• Sign: ILS with graphic
• Must hold unless cleared by ATC

1. MANDATORY INSTRUCTION: Red/White
2. LOCATION: Black/Yellow border
3. DIRECTION: Yellow/Black
4. DESTINATION: Yellow/Black
5. INFORMATION: Yellow/Black
6. RUNWAY DISTANCE REMAINING: Black/White

• RED background, WHITE text
• Must comply - no entry without clearance

Examples:
• Runway holding position: '15-33'
• ILS critical area
• No entry signs

Numbers arranged to match runway thresholds

• BLACK background, YELLOW text/border
• Identifies WHERE you are

Types:
• Taxiway location (e.g., 'A')
• Runway location (e.g., '27')
• Runway boundary (leaving runway)
• ILS critical area boundary

• YELLOW background, BLACK text
• Shows intersecting taxiways and directions
• Arrows indicate direction of turn
• Located before intersection
• Arranged clockwise from left
• May include location sign in array

• YELLOW background, BLACK text
• Shows route to specific destinations
• Always includes direction arrow

Common legends:
• APRON, FBO, GA, CARGO
• FUEL, TERM (terminal)
• Runway numbers (outbound)

• BLACK background, WHITE numbers
• Number = thousands of feet remaining
• '3' = 3,000 ft remaining
• Last sign ('1') at least 950 ft from end
• Located on one or both sides of runway

1. Aviation RED: Flashing beacons + steady lights (night)
2. Medium White: Flashing, day/twilight/night adjustable
3. High Intensity White: Flashing, all conditions
4. Dual: Red at night, white during day
5. Catenary: For transmission lines

• Located beyond runway end
• Crushes under aircraft weight
• Stops overruns safely
• Marked with yellow chevrons
• May be as close as 35 ft from runway end
• NEVER taxi or drive across EMAS!

• Yellow 'X' placed at each end
• Indicates runway/taxiway closed
• May be temporary or permanent
• Do NOT use closed surface
• Check NOTAMs for closure information

• Movement area: Under ATC control
• Non-movement area: NOT under ATC

Boundary marking:
• Yellow solid line (non-movement side)
• Yellow dashed line (movement side)
• Need clearance to enter movement area at towered airports

• Threshold not at runway beginning
• White arrows lead to threshold
• Area before threshold:
 - OK for taxi, takeoff, rollout
 - NOT for landing
• Threshold bar marks landing start point

• Painted circle with arrow
• Arrow aligned with checkpoint azimuth
• Located on apron/taxiway
• Sign shows:
 - VOR ID and course
 - 'VOR CHECK COURSE'
 - DME data if applicable

• Limited access security area
• Requires proper badge/ID
• Can include AOA or secured areas
• Unauthorized entry prohibited
• Subject to civil/criminal penalties
• Report suspicious activity: 866-427-3287

RED = STOP/MANDATORY (runway holding)
YELLOW background = Direction/Destination
BLACK background = Location (where you ARE)
BLACK with WHITE = Distance remaining

'Red means stop, Yellow means go (direction), Black tells you where you are'
